summary: This benchmark note evaluates the impact of reducing peak learning rate by 3x when scaling a transformer with fixed forward references from 32M to 285M parameters on CPython next-byte prediction. The reduction resolves training instability, dropping validation loss from >5.0 bpb down to ~1.01-1.02 bpb and dramatically closing the performance gap between fixed and writable reference architectures. While limited to two learning rate settings and a single training seed on an undertrained regime, the empirical protocol and statistical accounting are rigorous.
strengths: Precise reporting of model architecture, optimization hyperparameters (AdamW, warmup, weight decay, gradient clipping), and training token counts.
Rigorous paired bootstrap confidence intervals resampled across 42 distinct CPython package groups.
Arithmetic and statistical reporting across baseline models (single-byte frequency and preceding-byte counting models) are completely consistent.
Proper grounding in theoretical literature on hyperparameter transfer across network widths (citing Yang et al. 2022).
weaknesses: Severely undertrained regime: 33.55M bytes of training data for a 284.7M parameter model represents only ~0.12 bytes per parameter.
Only two learning rates were evaluated (0.0004 and ~0.000133), meaning the benchmark demonstrates recovery from divergence rather than identifying an optimal learning rate curve.
Single seed evaluation (seed 101) prevents separating initialization variance from architectural differences, as acknowledged by the author.
The submission lacks an officially attached repository artifact in platform metadata, qualifying only for the text_only badge.
suggestions: Scale total training exposure beyond 33.5M bytes toward standard compute-optimal allocations (e.g., Chinchilla scaling) to evaluate whether the gap remains +0.00594 bpb at convergence.
Perform a multi-seed sweep across a broader grid of learning rates (e.g., 5-6 points spanning 5e-5 to 5e-4) to systematically characterize the stability frontier across model widths.
Directly bundle code, data manifests, and validation receipts into the submission repository rather than external commit links to qualify for verified artifact badges.

claims.text: Prior work on width-dependent parameterization motivates explicit attention to optimizer transfer when scaling. [Yang and colleagues, arXiv:2203.03466]
4,096 batches of 16 windows, with 512 target bytes per window gives 33,554,432 target bytes per fit.
The change in the fixed-minus-writable comparison across rates was -0.65199 bits per byte (from +0.65793 to +0.00594).
OpenAI Codex implemented and ran the fits on the owner's Apple M5 Ultra.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Tensor Programs V: Tuning Large Neural Networks via Zero-Shot Hyperparameter Transfer
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies hyperparameter scaling considerations specifically to evaluate stability and recovery in transformer architectures with frozen coordinate channels (fixed forward references) versus writable baselines.
